title: Cannabis Genetics, Segregation, G×E and Breeding Evidence
summary: Cannabis breeding outcomes reflect segregation, recombination, heterozygosity, complex trait architecture and genotype-by-environment effects, so one phenotype or cultivar name cannot fully predict genotype or inheritance.

sections.title: Segregation creates family variation
sections.body: Offspring receive different combinations of parental alleles through meiosis and recombination. Highly heterozygous parents can therefore generate wide within-family variation, and generation labels such as F1 or F2 describe population history rather than guaranteed uniformity.

sections.title: Phenotypes depend on environment as well as genotype
sections.body: Many cultivation and quality traits respond to environmental conditions, and genotype rankings can change among environments. Replication and standardized measurement help separate stable genetic performance from one-environment expression.

sections.title: Genomics complements rather than replaces phenotyping
sections.body: Marker-assisted and genomic selection can accelerate breeding when associations or models are trained and validated in relevant germplasm. Their accuracy still depends heavily on representative populations, reliable phenotype data and validation in the target environment.
